steps.say: Painful rigid erections are treated as emergencies always. Ischemic priapism is staged as a compartment crisis. Corpora are turned rigid while the glans stays soft. Arterial inflow is absent on Doppler testing completely. Acidosis with hypoxia is staged progressing inside rapidly. Muscle death is counted in hours not days.
steps.tx: **Ischemic priapism** (painful low-flow erection), **low-flow priapism** (veno-occlusive trap), is a **compartment emergency** (penile compartment crisis) with rigid corpora, absent cavernosal inflow, and mounting acidosis with hypoxia. Treat the clock as muscle survival time. Aspirate and rescue without delay, because fibrosis starts within hours.

steps.say: Cavernosal gases are drawn to prove the diagnosis bedside. Blood is drawn from the corpus for analysis. Ischemic samples are matched to venous blood exactly. pH below seven point two five is staged as defining acidosis. Oxygen under thirty with carbon dioxide above sixty is recorded completing the picture. Bright red arterial blood is staged pointing the other way.
steps.tx: **Cavernosal blood gas** (penile blood test) in ischemia shows **pH <7.25** (acid below seven point two five), **pO2 <30 mmHg** (oxygen under thirty), and **pCO2 >60 mmHg** (carbon dioxide above sixty), matching ischemic venous blood. Draw gases before treatment to classify the crisis. Repeat after intervention, because numbers track rescue.

steps.say: Painless partial erections are watched differently. Non ischemic priapism is staged as arterial high flow. Blunt perineal trauma is blamed to start the leak. An arteriolar fistula is tapped feeding the sinusoids directly. The shaft is staged tumescent but never rigid. Doppler is used showing turbulent arterial jets inside.
steps.tx: **Non-ischemic priapism** (painless high-flow erection), **arterial priapism** (traumatic fistula leak), remains swollen yet soft when blunt perineal injury creates an **arteriolar fistula** (artery to sinusoid leak). Confirm turbulent arterial flow on Doppler. Manage mostly without emergency shunts, because ischemia is absent here.

steps.say: Aspiration with drugs is tried first always. Corporal aspiration is performed with saline irrigation. Phenylephrine is injected as the alpha one agonist. One hundred to five hundred mcg per mL is the listed strength. Doses are repeated every three to five minutes. Blood pressure with pulse is monitored throughout.
steps.tx: **Corporal aspiration** (needle drainage) with saline irrigation opens treatment, followed by intracavernosal **phenylephrine** (**alpha-1 agonist** (vessel tightening drug)) **100 to 500 mcg/mL** (one hundred to five hundred micrograms per millilitre) repeated every 3 to 5 minutes. Watch blood pressure and pulse with each dose, because systemic absorption spikes pressure.

steps.say: Failed drugs are followed by distal shunts promptly. Winter with Ebbehoj shunts are created percutaneously here. A large bore needle is passed connecting glans to corpora. Blood is drained from rigid chambers outward steadily. The procedures are staged at the bedside routinely. Erection is softened often within minutes afterwards.
steps.tx: **Winter shunt** (needle glans puncture) and **Ebbehoj shunt** (scalpel slit shunt), **distal shunt** (tip procedures), connect glans to corpora percutaneously for outflow. Pass a large bore needle or blade through glans into cavernosum. Compress afterwards and reassess rigidity, because flow must visibly improve.

steps.say: Open distal shunts are staged removing tissue cores here. Al-Ghorab with Burnett shunts are opened through the glans. A five mm disc of tunica is excised surgically. Outflow is restored through the window created widely. Bleeding is controlled with pressure dressing alone. Closure is performed in layers afterwards routinely.
steps.tx: **Al-Ghorab shunt** (open window shunt) and **Burnett shunt** (elliptical excision shunt) excise a **5 mm** (five millimetre) core of distal tunica through the glans for wider outflow. Close glans in layers over pressure dressing. Step up from needle shunts when rigidity persists, because bigger windows drain better.

steps.say: Proximal shunts are built near the perineum surgically. The Quackels shunt is sewn joining corpus to spongiosum surgically. The Grayhack shunt is grafted connecting saphenous vein to cavernosum. Both are staged when distal shunts fail completely. Wounds are closed with drains placed routinely. Patency is checked with Doppler afterwards.
steps.tx: **Quackels shunt** (corporospongiosal join) anastomoses corpus to spongiosum at the perineum, while **Grayhack shunt** (vein bypass shunt) joins saphenous vein to corpus cavernosum as a **proximal shunt** (base procedure). Reserve for failed distal shunts. Check patency with Doppler before leaving theatre, because early blockage needs revision.

steps.say: Long delays are staged killing erectile tissue outright. Ischemia beyond thirty six to forty eight hours is staged as necrotic. Smooth muscle is replaced by fibrosis completely. Natural erections are lost never to return afterwards. Immediate prosthesis insertion is offered to save length. The device resolves priapism while preventing shortening.
steps.tx: **Smooth muscle necrosis** (erectile tissue death) with fibrosis follows ischemia beyond **36 to 48 hours** (thirty six to forty eight hours), ending natural erectile function. **Immediate prosthesis** (early implant rescue) insertion resolves the priapism and preserves penile length. Do not wait for fibrosis to mature, because delayed implants shorten and complicate.
